problem: "Release it and the charge reverses" contradicts the chapter's own law Q = dF. Charge is proportional to the applied stress, so removing the force brings the charge back to zero, not to an opposite value. A student will read this as: pressing gives +Q and releasing gives −Q.
fix: Remove the force and the charge falls back to zero. The charge reverses sign only if the force is reversed in direction, that is, if the plate is stretched instead of compressed.

where: Section 1, formula V = g t P
problem: The formula writes g = d/ε but ε is never defined; εr appears in the material list and ε0 only appears later in Section 2.
fix: Add: ε is the permittivity of the crystal, ε = ε0 εr, with ε0 = 8.85×10⁻¹² F/m and εr the relative permittivity (4.5 for quartz).

problem: The d33 / d31 labelling is stated as if it holds for every crystal. Those subscripts belong to poled materials such as PZT and PVDF; quartz is not poled and its datasheet quotes d11 (and d14).
fix: Say: for poled ceramics and polymer films a datasheet gives d33 for force along the poling axis and d31 for force at right angles to it; for quartz the quoted coefficient is d11.

problem: The text says a stack of crystal plates converts pressure to force and then uses q = dAP. In a stack of n plates the charges add, so the formula underestimates the output by a factor n.
fix: Write q = n d A P for a stack of n plates (n = 1 for a single diaphragm), so Vout = −n d A P / Cf.
